newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ghana sees continuing gold output growth.
newsitem.headline: Ghana sees continuing gold output growth.

text.p: Ghana's gold exports will continue to rise with the opening of more mines, use of state-of-the-art mining technology and the arrival of more prospectors, according to a Ghana Minerals Commission document.
The number of registered gold companies rose to 217 after 30 newcomers were licensed in 1996, said the GMC document which was sent to the state Ghana News Agency on Thursday.

There were 74 foreign mining companies and 123 Ghanaian-owned companies in 1996 -- with 17 new registrations. Four more companies with leasing rights were also registered, taking the number to 20, it said.
The document put annual investments in the gold sector at around $200 million, with earnings at around $650 million.
Gold production had risen by 500 percent over the past decade, it said.
Ghana's Chamber of Mines puts 1996 gold production by its 134 members at 1.5 million ounces, against 1.2 million ounces in 1995.
Sources at Ghana's mining colossus Ashanti Goldfields Company Limited say the company alone aims to produce over a million ounces of gold in 1997, against 940,000 ounces in 1996.
"The emphasis is now more on productivity," one industry source said, referring to a drive at AGC to cut operating costs after unspectacular profits in the early 1990s.
